title: Legal Discovery Intelligence Graph
summary: A deployed Graph RAG investigation workspace with cited evidence, entity graphs, and reproducible evaluation.
outcome: A public synthetic-matter investigation workflow combines vector and graph retrieval, cited evidence, timelines, privilege/PII flags, calibrated refusal, and an auditable case brief.

deployment.runtime: Flask + gunicorn with an ONNX embedding backend

metrics: Entity-mention extraction micro F1 0.887 strict on the 455-document synthetic corpus
Hybrid retrieval R@10 0.857 on the committed dense-corpus evaluation
Relationship-query hit@5 improved from 0.500 vector-only to 0.833 with graph expansion
Privilege and synthetic-PII flag F1 1.0 on clean templated text
stages: Deterministic synthetic corpus and gold-label generation
Real-file ingestion for PDF, DOCX, and EML
Entity, event, privilege, and synthetic-PII extraction
PostgreSQL pgvector indexing and Neo4j graph loading
Hybrid retrieval with calibrated refusal and cited evidence
Flask investigation UI with graph, timeline, evaluation, and case brief
architecture: Synthetic discovery corpus and gold labels
Hybrid evidence retriever and refusal policy
evaluation: artifacts/extraction_metrics.json records strict and relaxed span-matching metrics against emitted gold labels
artifacts/retrieval_metrics.json records vector-only and graph-expanded retrieval by query category and k
artifacts/flags_metrics.json records document-level privilege and synthetic-PII rule results
The repository documents the dense-corpus regressions and warns that templated synthetic text overstates real-world performance
operationalTradeoffs: Graph expansion materially improves relationship hit@5 but can dilute some dense-corpus results at larger k
The Render free tier sleeps, has a constrained memory envelope, and requires an ONNX backend rather than torch
The public app is deliberately read-only and synthetic; real eDiscovery would require access control, matter isolation, OCR, retention, and legal/privacy review
A public HTTP response is verified, but this is not an availability, confidentiality, or production-SLO claim
disclaimer: All documents, people, companies, amounts, identifiers, and events are synthetic and fictional. Metrics are reproducible results on templated synthetic text and are not claims about real legal matters, privilege determinations, or production discovery performance.

presentation.question: How can an investigator move from a large discovery record to evidence they can inspect and trace?
presentation.answer: Model the corpus through complementary vector and graph retrieval, preserve provenance at every hop, and refuse when the evidence threshold is not met.
presentation.decisionSupported: Whether a relationship or event is supported by cited evidence in the fictional matter.
presentation.architectureAlt: System architecture showing a reviewer, synthetic discovery inputs, validation and extraction, vector and graph stores, hybrid retrieval, security boundary, observability, Render deployment, cited outputs, and the evaluation loop.
presentation.evaluationMode: deterministic local evaluation on a synthetic corpus plus a live reachability observation

story.recruiterSummary: Legal discovery teams need to connect people, events, documents, and evidence without losing the source trail. This project demonstrates that workflow on a fully fictional matter: reviewers can search, traverse relationships, inspect a timeline, and open cited documents while the product clearly distinguishes evidence from generated structure.
story.technicalNarrative: A deterministic generator emits a 455-document corpus and gold labels. Offline pipelines extract entities/events, create pgvector embeddings, and load Neo4j relationships. The deployed Flask app uses an ONNX embedding backend within Render's memory limit, fuses vector and graph retrieval, applies a calibrated refusal threshold, and renders cited results, graphs, timelines, flags, and evaluation artifacts.

title: Legal Document Intelligence RAG
summary: A deployed Azure RAG research workspace for citation-grounded questions over public M&A litigation and transaction documents.
outcome: A versioned public-document pipeline turns court opinions and SEC filings into 3,055 searchable chunks and returns evidence-linked answers with an explicit refusal path.

deployment.runtime: Flask and Gunicorn on Azure App Service with managed identity, Azure AI Search, and Blob Storage

metrics: Retrieval hit rate@8 1.0 on the 45-question gold-qa-v2-delaware-expansion benchmark
Citation-provenance validity 1.0 on the same versioned benchmark
3,055 public chunks in the promoted r3 Azure AI Search index
stages: Public source registration and checksum validation
Azure Document Intelligence and native SEC HTML extraction
Read-only Flask research workspace on Azure App Service
architecture: Public court opinions and SEC transaction documents
Versioned extraction adapters and document records
Flask evidence workspace with source links
evaluation: data/evaluation/latest.json records the 45-question gold-qa-v2-delaware-expansion release evaluation
Retrieval hit rate and citation provenance measure corpus retrieval and citation traceability, not legal-answer correctness
The release runbook requires corpus, retrieval, citation, refusal, and post-deployment route checks
operationalTradeoffs: Azure managed services simplify identity and hosted retrieval but add cloud-resource cost and release coordination
The public endpoint is anonymous and read-only; it is not a confidential eDiscovery workspace or production legal service
The current evaluation proves retrieval and provenance, not attorney-reviewed answer accuracy
The promoted r3 index has a separately retained r2 rollback index
disclaimer: Uses public court opinions and public SEC transaction documents. The application provides legal information for engineering demonstration and is not legal advice.

presentation.question: How can legal research return an evidence-linked answer without wandering beyond an approved public corpus?
presentation.answer: Register and checksum the source boundary, preserve document structure, retrieve only from the promoted index, and require citations or an explicit refusal.
presentation.decisionSupported: Whether the public corpus contains retrievable, traceable evidence for the research question.
presentation.architectureAlt: System architecture showing a legal researcher, registered public court and SEC sources, checksum validation, extraction, chunk storage, Azure AI Search, Azure OpenAI, managed identity, observability, deployment, cited output, and evaluation.
presentation.evaluationMode: versioned integration evaluation against the promoted public retrieval index plus a live reachability observation

story.recruiterSummary: Legal teams need answers that stay attached to the source, especially when documents are long and high stakes. This project demonstrates an evidence-first research workflow over public M&A litigation and transaction documents: a reviewer asks a question, receives a grounded answer, and can inspect the cited document, section, and page rather than trusting an unsupported response.
story.technicalNarrative: Versioned adapters ingest public PDFs through Azure Document Intelligence and public SEC HTML through a native parser, normalize them into stable records, and build structure-aware chunks. Azure AI Search retrieves the promoted public corpus; Azure OpenAI generates only from that evidence, while the Flask workspace exposes research, corpus, evaluation, and health views. Managed identity separates deployed resources from local credentials, and the corpus index is promoted independently from application deployment.

title: Text-to-SQL Interface with Guardrails and Hallucination Detection
summary: An approval-gated analyst console that turns bounded natural-language questions into policy-checked, read-only SQL over disclosed synthetic data.
outcome: Reviewers can inspect SQL, assumptions, schema lineage, policy checks, and a bounded result preview before one single-use execution; unsafe, malformed, identifier-exposing, and hallucinated-schema queries fail closed.

deployment.runtime: Scale-to-zero FastAPI container using the committed demo fixture and ephemeral SQLite proposal state

metrics: 18 of 18 deterministic local evaluation cases matched their expected trusted or refused outcome
100% safety-rejection rate across the committed unsafe-policy evaluation cases
100% hallucination-detection rate across the committed unknown-table and unknown-column cases
6 status-only public route, fixture-boundary, and deployed-control checks passed on the anonymous live demo
stages: Curated semantic catalog and explicit data classification
Azure OpenAI SQL proposal generation through Microsoft Entra ID
Parser-backed table, column, function, statement, and resource policy checks
Human review with short-lived single-use approval
Policy and snapshot revalidation before read-only DuckDB execution
Bounded result preview with privacy-preserving lifecycle events
architecture: Azure OpenAI proposal adapter using managed identity
SQLGlot policy engine and DuckDB EXPLAIN
Read-only DuckDB execution over a hand-authored synthetic demo fixture
evaluation: evaluation/report.json is regenerated from the committed fixture and records 18 deterministic policy cases
The public verification record checks root, evaluation, examples, safe preview, and the active demo-fixture boundary without retaining SQL or result rows
A separate local Entra-authenticated proposal-to-approved-execution lifecycle is integration evidence, not a production benchmark
operationalTradeoffs: Anonymous access makes recruiter review easy but provides no caller identity or authorization boundary
The deployed rate, proposal-budget, and counter controls are process-local and reset after scale-to-zero or restart
SQLite under /tmp is appropriate only for the zero-to-one-replica anonymous demo because proposal state is lost on scale-to-zero or restart and cannot coordinate replicas
The committed fixture keeps synthetic join identifiers internally, while model context and result previews exclude identifier-like fields
Local latency and cost observations are not production SLO or cost claims
disclaimer: Anonymous, non-production demonstration using synthetic data only. It is not a bank system, fraud decision service, security posture, availability claim, or production-readiness claim.

presentation.question: How can analysts use natural-language SQL proposals without letting model output execute unchecked?
presentation.answer: Separate proposal from execution, expose assumptions and lineage, enforce parser-backed policy, require short-lived human approval, and revalidate before one bounded read-only preview.
presentation.decisionSupported: Whether a proposed analytical query is within the classified schema and safe enough for one reviewed execution.
presentation.architectureAlt: System architecture showing an analyst, synthetic data and semantic catalog, FastAPI proposal and approval interfaces, Azure OpenAI, SQLGlot and DuckDB validation, ephemeral approval storage, read-only execution, privacy boundary, telemetry, deployment controls, and evaluation.
presentation.evaluationMode: deterministic local policy evaluation plus live status-only integration checks on an anonymous demo

story.recruiterSummary: Natural-language analytics is attractive because it lowers the barrier to data access, but executing model-generated SQL directly creates obvious security, privacy, and correctness risk. This project turns that risky shortcut into a reviewable workflow: the model may propose, a deterministic policy engine must validate, and a person must approve one bounded read-only preview.
story.technicalNarrative: FastAPI separates proposal from execution. Azure OpenAI receives only an identifier-excluding semantic catalog through Microsoft Entra authentication; SQLGlot checks statement shape, functions, tables, columns, identifier projection, and ranking semantics; DuckDB EXPLAIN and resource limits run before a short-lived approval can be consumed. Execution revalidates both SQL policy and the active snapshot checksum.
scalabilityRoadmap: Replace ephemeral SQLite with an owner-approved transactional store and prove cross-replica single-use consumption
Enable single-tenant Microsoft Entra authentication and verify unauthenticated denial
Replace process-local rate and proposal budgets with durable distributed controls before multi-replica hosting
Add alerting, budget ownership, availability/error monitoring, and an owner-approved load envelope
Expand semantic evaluation with reviewer-approved equivalent SQL rather than literal query matching
story.executiveSummary: A guarded Text-to-SQL first demo that makes model output inspectable, evidence-linked, and explicitly non-production.
